eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from PAGASA highlight the southwest monsoon (habagat) driving cloudy skies, scattered rainshowers, and thunderstorms over Metro Manila on August 18, with an official high of 32°C but a 60% rain probability that favors suppressed afternoon maxima. Persistent cloud cover and precipitation limit solar heating and evaporative cooling effects, positioning 28°C as the market leader at 44.5% implied probability, followed by 27°C, consistent with historical August patterns where monsoon days often yield highs 2–4°C below the 30–31°C seasonal average. Model consensus from multiple sources shows limited intensification potential ahead of the event, with traders weighting near-term observational data on humidity and wind patterns. Updated PAGASA briefings tomorrow morning represent the key data release that could shift these odds.

Latest guidance from MetService and international models shows overcast skies, light drizzle, and maximum temperatures of 10–11°C on the 19th, with overnight minima in the 6–8°C range. A recent pulse of cooler polar air has kept regional temperatures near or slightly below seasonal norms, consistent with NIWA’s June–August outlook favoring near-average conditions. Stronger winds and continued marine influence further cap any potential for warmer readings above 12°C, while the absence of clear-sky radiative heating or northerly advection makes sub-10°C outcomes unlikely. Traders have therefore concentrated probability on the narrow 10–12°C band, with 11°C capturing the central tendency of the latest model runs. Updated official forecasts on the morning of the 18th or 19th will provide the final inputs for market resolution.
